source: Frozen libsodium-wrappers-sumo crypto_kdf_derive_from_key output for the (context, subkey_id) pairs declared in types.ts. Same trust-class as @truecairn/crypto's kdf-subkey KAT — verifies that the master key is being fed through the correct domain separators with the correct ids, and would catch any silent change to KDF_CONTEXT_AUDIT, KDF_CONTEXT_WRAP, KDF_CONTEXT_VAULT_CAPTURE, KDF_SUBKEY_ID_AUDIT_SIGNING, KDF_SUBKEY_ID_TIER_WRAPPING or KDF_SUBKEY_ID_VAULT_CAPTURE.

vaultCapture.note: docs/34 — the owner's write-only capture keypair. The PUBLIC key is pinned as well as the seed because it is the value that actually leaves the browser and reaches a phone: a derivation change that altered it would strand every capture already sealed to the old key, and pinning only the seed would not catch a change in how the keypair is built from that seed.

contactBindingV2.comment: Per-relationship contact seeds (v2). root = crypto_kdf_derive_from_key(masterKey, ctx='tc-cbind', subkey_id=1, len=32); seed = BLAKE2b(key=root, msg=utf8(purpose + relationshipId), outlen=32) with purpose 'x25519:' or 'ed25519:'. Two relationships are pinned deliberately: one proves determinism, two prove UNLINKABILITY — the property the whole change exists for, and the one a naive reimplementation (ignoring relationshipId, or appending it instead of prefixing the purpose) would silently lose while still passing a single-vector check.

contactPin.note: F1+F2 (PLAN-v1-launch.md §1.2). The master-derived key that encrypts contact display labels and key pins, moving them off the S1 TIER key — which is sealed to the S1 beneficiary and unsealed in their browser on release, so it let one recipient read the owner's private labels for every contact, including S2/S3-only ones. Context is 'tc-cmeta', NOT the plan's 'tc-cpin': that string is 7 bytes and crypto_kdf_derive_from_key requires exactly 8, so the plan's name throws at the first call. Pinned because a silent change to the context or subkey id would re-derive a different key and make every stored label unreadable.
